root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 introduced two transformations to pdf_to_markdown_docling that are the ONLY code changes between Run 12 and Run 13 affecting markdown content: (1) _repair_docling_tables wrapping every export_to_markdown() call (converters.py:2388-2458, applied at lines 2627,2697,2991), and (2) NFKC normalization of Arabic Presentation Forms in _pre_inference_normalize (converters.py:2197-2200). Both SLA and marsoom-13 are Arabic PDFs flat-routed (tree <3 nodes). In Run 12, route_and_extract_flat produced 264 and 6 blocks respectively. In Run 13, 0 blocks. The markdown is non-empty (doc_description populates from metadata), but route_and_extract_flat produces zero parseable blocks from it — all content ends up skipped (likely via fence-toggle, HR-separator, or empty-line paths). The exact interaction causing total block loss needs per-document markdown comparison. qerar-106 shows a different pattern (truncation at Article 4, 179->11 nodes) but shares the Arabic extraction context.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:_repair_docling_tables (2388-2458) + converters.py:_pre_inference_normalize NFKC (2197-2200) -> pdf_to_markdown_docling (2627,2697) -> client.py:md_content -> flat routing -> route_and_extract_flat
root_causes.suggested_fix: Compare the markdown output of pdf_to_markdown_docling for the SLA doc with and without _repair_docling_tables and NFKC normalization (toggle via env vars RFC029_TABLE_DEDUP_ENABLED=0 and conditionalizing the NFKC block). Identify which transformation produces markdown that route_and_extract_flat cannot parse into blocks. Then fix the specific interaction — likely a table-row formatting change that causes the flat parser to misclassify content lines.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 added 4 new validate_tree failure reasons (suspect_density, low_content_density, empty_node_contamination, arabic_low_content_ratio) in helpers.py but NONE are handled in client.py's recovery/routing paths. OCR escalation only handles garbling/node_garbling/visual_order_garble. Flat routing only handles node_count<3/depth<2. These new reasons fall through to raise LowQualityTreeError (ERROR) with NO recovery opportunity. For docs in THIS cluster the tree has <3 nodes so node_count<3 fires first (before suspect_density), but the gap is systemic and explains the 3 ERROR docs in the audit (Penal Code, federal_decree_law_no_33, marsoom_33). For the SLA doc (20 pages, ~27k chars = ~1394 chars/page < 1500 threshold), suspect_density WOULD fire if the tree had >=3 nodes.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:validate_tree (1330-1375 new gates) -> client.py:index (1381-1639 — none of the 4 new reasons match flat routing or OCR escalation conditions)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add the new validate_tree failure reasons to either the OCR escalation condition or the flat routing condition in client.py. suspect_density and low_content_density should route to flat (reason='node_count<3') since the tree has content but is structurally rejected. empty_node_contamination should attempt OCR escalation. arabic_low_content_ratio should attempt OCR escalation.

root_causes.root_cause: Docling TableFormer cannot extract vector-icon table cells (checkmarks/symbols rendered as PDF path operators, not Unicode text glyphs). The Unfallversicherung benefit-comparison tables have empty_cell_ratio 0.44-0.75 because cell content is rasterized vector icons invisible to text-layer extraction. This predates RFC-029 and has persisted across all runs (Run 11, 12, 13). No RFC-029 change addresses this; _repair_docling_tables processes table FORMAT (dedup, whitespace) but cannot recover content Docling never extracted.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:pdf_to_markdown_docling -> Docling TableFormer ACCURATE mode -> export_to_markdown() (checkmark glyphs lost at extraction) -> helpers.py:_flat_parse_table -> helpers.py:flag_empty_cells
root_causes.suggested_fix: Cell-level rasterization+OCR for table cells with zero text content but non-zero visual content (vector-icon path operators). Alternative: Docling upstream enhancement for path-operator glyph recognition. RFC-010 originally scoped this; RFC-027 deferred it.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D5c (post-Docling chart-page-detection heuristic) was marked complete in tasks-rfc029 but never implemented in code. No function for chart-page density detection or PictureItem synthesis exists anywhere in the codebase. Without D5c, Docling's Heron RT-DETRv2 layout model does not classify vector charts/bar-charts as PictureItem, so zero <!-- image --> markers are emitted and _recover_picture_results returns [] at converters.py:2225 (guard: _IMAGE_MARKER not in md). The entire picture enrichment pipeline never runs for chart-dominant PDF pages.
root_causes.code_path: converters.py:2225 -> _recover_picture_results entry guard (_IMAGE_MARKER in md) -> returns [] because Docling never emitted markers for chart pages
root_causes.suggested_fix: Implement D5c as designed in RFC-029: add a post-Docling heuristic that detects pages with very low text content relative to page area (<200 chars/page but known visual content from page dimensions/aspect ratio) and synthesizes PictureItem regions for them so they enter the existing picture-enrichment pipeline. This requires page rendering + text-density calculation + threshold tuning.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D1 low_content_density gate in validate_tree (helpers.py:1342-1356) rejects trees with chars_per_node < 500 when total_nodes >= 200. This new gate was introduced in commit 08b6eea and has no recovery path -- low_content_density is not in the OCR escalation reasons list (client.py:1008), so the tree simply ERRORs. The threshold of 500 chars/node is too aggressive for legal documents with fine-grained article structure: Penal Code (606 nodes, 408.2 chars/node) and marsoom-33-AR (231 nodes, 459.4 chars/node) were previously healthy PASS trees with near-identical metrics. For federal_decree_law_no_33 EN the drop from ~221 to 54.3 chars/node suggests additional over-fragmentation from _repair_docling_tables char reduction (table whitespace stripping reduced total chars while node count held or grew).
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py::validate_tree -> low_content_density gate (line 1349)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Two changes: (1) Add low_content_density to the OCR escalation reasons list in client.py:1008 so the tree gets a recovery attempt instead of immediately ERRORing. (2) Either lower the threshold from 500 to ~200 chars/node (legal articles averaging 300-450 chars/node are legitimate), or raise the node-count floor from 200 to a higher value (e.g., 500) that only catches truly degenerate over-fragmented trees. The docstring at line 1289 says 'total_nodes >= 3' but code uses >= 200 -- fix the docstring too.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D3 fence stripping in route_and_extract_flat (helpers.py:2720-2726) strips ALL content inside fenced code blocks. Docling wraps substantial Arabic document content in fenced blocks for the MOU document, causing 89% content loss (166 nodes/13564 chars -> 20 nodes/1487 chars). The garble gate misfire (ratio=1.00) is a CONSEQUENCE: the truncated preamble has concentrated mixed-script patterns that trip _has_sparse_mojibake or _is_garbled_blob checks which were diluted in the full-length text.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:route_and_extract_flat -> fence stripping loop (in_fence toggle on ``` lines) -> all fenced content silently dropped
root_causes.suggested_fix: Change fence stripping from content-dropping to delimiter-only stripping: instead of skipping ALL lines inside fences, skip only the ``` delimiter lines themselves and let the enclosed content fall through to the normal prose/table parsers. Alternatively, add a content-length guard: only strip fenced blocks below a character threshold (e.g. <50 chars) that are likely formatting noise, preserving substantial content blocks.

root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:_garble_check_nodes -> node.get('text') only, skips node.get('title')

Wire the existing _word_has_reversed_morphology check into the title inspection path so reversed Arabic titles are detected.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D6 Phase B judge calibration rules were marked complete (task 1.7) but never actually written to .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md. The skill file (lines 34-42) still only contains the old RFC-028 D6 guidance about image markers in hierarchical docs. The two new rules specified by RFC-029 D6 are missing: (1) stability rule -- when stored gate verdict is PASS and metrics are byte-identical to the prior run, the judge MUST NOT downgrade unless citing a specific new defect; (2) severity-anchoring rule -- for flat/chart docs with <1000 chars and zero enrichments, anchor severity to MARGINAL (not FAIL) when extraction has not regressed. Without these rules, the Opus judge applies inconsistent scrutiny across runs to byte-identical content: Haftpflicht (stored PASS, 132 nodes/53K chars, depth 2 unchanged) gets downgraded to MARGINAL on 'depth-2-too-shallow' scrutiny the Run 12 judge did not apply; image pie chart (stored MARGINAL, 6 nodes/489 chars byte-identical) gets escalated to FAIL on RTL garbling the Run 12 judge did not flag. Both regressions are pure judge non-determinism with no underlying pipeline change.
root_causes.code_path: .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md lines 34-42 (Judge Verdict guidance section)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add the two RFC-029 D6 calibration rules to .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md after the existing RFC-028 D6 paragraph: (1) Stability rule: 'When stored gate verdict is PASS and extraction metrics (node count, char count, depth) are within 10% of the prior run, the judge MUST NOT downgrade unless it can cite a specific content-quality defect (garbling, content loss, structural corruption) not present in the prior run finding. Known persistent limitations (e.g. shallow depth for a complex document) that were tolerated in the prior run are NOT grounds for downgrade.' (2) Severity-anchoring rule: 'For flat/chart-heavy docs (content_class starts with flat_) with <1000 total chars and zero picture enrichments, anchor severity to MARGINAL (not FAIL) when the extraction layer has not regressed -- the missing enrichment is a known pipeline gap, not a per-run regression.' Also add a consistency check note to .claude/skills/corpus-score-diff/SKILL.md for byte-identical artifacts across runs.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D2 added suspect_density check to validate_tree (chars_per_page < 1500 floor with page_count threading). For warid-597 (42-page scanned Arabic PDF, 54728 chars / 42 pages = 1303 chars/page < 1500), this fires and returns (False, 'suspect_density'). But 'suspect_density' is not handled by ANY recovery or routing path in client.py -- not in OCR escalation triggers (garbling/node_garbling/visual_order_garble), not in flat routing (node_count<3/depth<2), not in VLM fallback. Falls through to LowQualityTreeError raise at line 1639. In Run 12, the tree PASSED validate_tree (garble gate blind to numeric-junk) and was persisted. RFC-029 design intended verdict change to MARGINAL/FAIL, not ERROR.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:validate_tree (line 1359-1365) -> client.py (line 1381-1387, reason not in flat routing set) -> client.py (line 1637-1639, raises LowQualityTreeError)

Change: reason in ('node_count<3', 'depth<2') to include these new reasons. This routes rejected trees to flat extraction (which matches RFC-029 D1 design intent) instead of raising LowQualityTreeError. Alternatively, move the suspect_density check from validate_tree to classify_verdict so the tree is persisted but gets a lower verdict.

root_causes.root_cause: _segment_table_nodes (helpers.py:2307) was implemented in RFC-029 D7 but only wired into the OCR retry path (client.py:1066) and VLM fallback path (client.py:1215). It is NOT called in the primary tree-build path (client.py:981 only calls split_oversized_leaf_nodes). GHV-TKV-Tarif goes through the primary path (no garble/OCR escalation), so _segment_table_nodes never runs and the tariff table stays merged in a single oversized node.

root_causes.suggested_fix: Add result['structure'] = _segment_table_nodes(result.get('structure', [])) at line 982 (after split_oversized_leaf_nodes, before validate_tree) in the primary tree-build path, matching the pattern already used in the OCR retry path at line 1066.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D3 fence stripping in route_and_extract_flat (helpers.py:2720-2726) strips ALL content inside fenced code blocks. Docling wraps substantial Arabic document content in fenced blocks for the MOU document, causing 89% content loss (166 nodes/13564 chars -> 20 nodes/1487 chars). The garble gate misfire (ratio=1.00) is a CONSEQUENCE: the truncated preamble has concentrated mixed-script patterns that trip _has_sparse_mojibake or _is_garbled_blob checks which were diluted in the full-length text.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:route_and_extract_flat -> fence stripping loop (in_fence toggle on ``` lines) -> all fenced content silently dropped
root_causes.suggested_fix: Change fence stripping from content-dropping to delimiter-only stripping: instead of skipping ALL lines inside fences, skip only the ``` delimiter lines themselves and let the enclosed content fall through to the normal prose/table parsers. Alternatively, add a content-length guard: only strip fenced blocks below a character threshold (e.g. <50 chars) that are likely formatting noise, preserving substantial content blocks.

root_causes.root_cause: _garble_check_nodes (helpers.py:1153-1186) only inspects node.get('text'), never node.get('title'). RTL-reversed titles (23/24 nodes in سياسة حوكمة) are invisible to the garble gate. classify_verdict also uses _tree_is_garbled which flattens only text fields via _flatten_tree_text. The garble gate has zero coverage of the title field, making title-level corruption a permanent blind spot.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:_garble_check_nodes -> node.get('text') only, skips node.get('title')
root_causes.suggested_fix: Extend _garble_check_nodes to also check node.get('title') for garble/RTL-reversal. Add title text to the _flatten_tree_text concatenation (or a separate title-aware flatten). Wire the existing _word_has_reversed_morphology check into the title inspection path so reversed Arabic titles are detected.

root_causes.root_cause: _check_bidi_coherence (helpers.py) is defined TWICE (lines 936 and 1028) but never called from any pipeline path. RFC-029 D0 intended this function to detect visual-order Arabic (reversed morphology) as a validate_tree gate, but the wiring was never completed. Both documents in this cluster would benefit from bidi coherence checking - the MOU for detecting reversed Arabic in body text, and سياسة حوكمة for detecting reversed Arabic in titles.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:_check_bidi_coherence (dead code, defined twice, never called)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Remove the duplicate definition. Wire the single _check_bidi_coherence into validate_tree as an additive gate (after _tree_is_rtl_reversed), returning (False, 'visual_order_garble') when the check fails. Add 'visual_order_garble' to the client.py flat-routing whitelist if bidi-incoherent docs should fall back to flat rather than ERROR.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D6 Phase B judge calibration rules were marked complete (task 1.7) but never actually written to .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md. The skill file (lines 34-42) still only contains the old RFC-028 D6 guidance about image markers in hierarchical docs. The two new rules specified by RFC-029 D6 are missing: (1) stability rule -- when stored gate verdict is PASS and metrics are byte-identical to the prior run, the judge MUST NOT downgrade unless citing a specific new defect; (2) severity-anchoring rule -- for flat/chart docs with <1000 chars and zero enrichments, anchor severity to MARGINAL (not FAIL) when extraction has not regressed. Without these rules, the Opus judge applies inconsistent scrutiny across runs to byte-identical content: Haftpflicht (stored PASS, 132 nodes/53K chars, depth 2 unchanged) gets downgraded to MARGINAL on 'depth-2-too-shallow' scrutiny the Run 12 judge did not apply; image pie chart (stored MARGINAL, 6 nodes/489 chars byte-identical) gets escalated to FAIL on RTL garbling the Run 12 judge did not flag. Both regressions are pure judge non-determinism with no underlying pipeline change.
root_causes.code_path: .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md lines 34-42 (Judge Verdict guidance section)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add the two RFC-029 D6 calibration rules to .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md after the existing RFC-028 D6 paragraph: (1) Stability rule: 'When stored gate verdict is PASS and extraction metrics (node count, char count, depth) are within 10% of the prior run, the judge MUST NOT downgrade unless it can cite a specific content-quality defect (garbling, content loss, structural corruption) not present in the prior run finding. Known persistent limitations (e.g. shallow depth for a complex document) that were tolerated in the prior run are NOT grounds for downgrade.' (2) Severity-anchoring rule: 'For flat/chart-heavy docs (content_class starts with flat_) with <1000 total chars and zero picture enrichments, anchor severity to MARGINAL (not FAIL) when the extraction layer has not regressed -- the missing enrichment is a known pipeline gap, not a per-run regression.' Also add a consistency check note to .claude/skills/corpus-score-diff/SKILL.md for byte-identical artifacts across runs.

root_causes.root_cause: RFC-029 D2 added suspect_density check to validate_tree (chars_per_page < 1500 floor with page_count threading). For warid-597 (42-page scanned Arabic PDF, 54728 chars / 42 pages = 1303 chars/page < 1500), this fires and returns (False, 'suspect_density'). But 'suspect_density' is not handled by ANY recovery or routing path in client.py -- not in OCR escalation triggers (garbling/node_garbling/visual_order_garble), not in flat routing (node_count<3/depth<2), not in VLM fallback. Falls through to LowQualityTreeError raise at line 1639. In Run 12, the tree PASSED validate_tree (garble gate blind to numeric-junk) and was persisted. RFC-029 design intended verdict change to MARGINAL/FAIL, not ERROR.
root_causes.code_path: helpers.py:validate_tree (line 1359-1365) -> client.py (line 1381-1387, reason not in flat routing set) -> client.py (line 1637-1639, raises LowQualityTreeError)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add 'suspect_density' (and other new RFC-029 validate_tree reasons: 'arabic_low_content_ratio', 'low_content_density', 'empty_node_contamination') to the flat routing path's reason check at client.py line 1387. Change: reason in ('node_count<3', 'depth<2') to include these new reasons. This routes rejected trees to flat extraction (which matches RFC-029 D1 design intent) instead of raising LowQualityTreeError. Alternatively, move the suspect_density check from validate_tree to classify_verdict so the tree is persisted but gets a lower verdict.
